name: psychological_level_mean_reversion
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, retail options traders and semi-institutional participants densely cluster stop-loss orders and protective limit orders at round 100-multiple levels (24000, 24100, 23900, etc.) because financial media and brokerage platforms display these levels as natural reference points. When NIFTY briefly pierces below a 100-multiple by 5-15 index points, it triggers stop-loss cascades and sweeps resting sell orders — but this selling is quickly absorbed by resting limit buy orders placed by VWAP-benchmarked algorithms and market makers who recognise the level as significant. The absorption creates a sharp snapback within 30-90 seconds: the very mechanism that caused the overshoot (stop hunting) ensures the subsequent reversal is fast and clean. At 5-second resolution we detect the pierce (price within 0.06% of the round level, just below it) combined with 3-minute RSI exhaustion below 35, entering as the bounce begins rather than waiting for a full bar confirmation.

indicators.name: round_level_100
indicators.purpose: Nearest 100-multiple level — no lookback needed, computed bar-by-bar. NIFTY at 24000-25000 range has 100-multiples every 0.4-0.5% apart, appearing 2-4 times per session as price oscillates within a 150-200pt daily range.

indicators.name: dist_signed
indicators.purpose: Signed distance from the nearest 100-multiple: positive = price above level, negative = price below. Magnitude < pierce_threshold indicates a near-level pierce is in progress. Directionality of sign determines whether to buy CE (below level, expect upward snap) or buy PE (above level, expect downward snap).

indicators.name: rsi_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute RSI (36 bars × 5s = 180s). NOT 12x scaled from original RSI(14) on 1-min bars — 14 × 12 = 168 bars (14 minutes) would be far too slow for a 30-90s trade. Instead, 36 bars captures short-term selling exhaustion within the last 3 minutes: if NIFTY has been declining for 3 minutes and now touches a round level, RSI < 35 confirms the near-term selloff is overextended. This is the TRIGGER window, not a trend-context filter. 36 bars is the minimum reliable RSI period that smooths out the 5-second noise while remaining sensitive enough to flag exhaustion before the bounce starts.

conditions: abs(dist_signed) / close < pierce_threshold_pct (within 0.06% of level, default 14-15 NIFTY pts at 24000)
rsi_36 < rsi_oversold (3-min RSI below 35 = short-term exhaustion)
buy_ce.confirmation: All conditions must be true on the same 5-second bar — no multi-bar confirmation needed since RSI itself provides the exhaustion filter

conditions: rsi_36 > rsi_overbought (3-min RSI above 65 = short-term overbought)
buy_pe.confirmation: All conditions must be true on the same 5-second bar

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points (~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5): if NIFTY moves 8 pts FURTHER away from the round level after entry, the stop-hunt thesis is wrong and the move is trending, not reverting — a 30-60 second reversion signal should not tolerate more than 8 spot pt adverse excursion (typical 30s NIFTY move is 2-5 pts, so 8 pts represents a clean trend break at this horizon).
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points (~14 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5): a round-level snapback on NIFTY typically covers 10-20 spot points in the first 60-90 seconds before stalling at the next micro-resistance. Targeting 14 spot points captures ~70% of the lower-end reversal (1:1.75 risk-reward at 4 stop vs 7 target).

filters.vix_filter: none — round-level reversions are behavioral and occur in both low and high volatility regimes
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:20 IST; skip first 5 minutes (09:15-09:20) to avoid opening auction noise where price discovery is erratic
filters.volume_filter: none — index volume bars are pre-aggregated and noisy at 5s; not reliable as a filter
filters.trend_filter: none — mean reversion at round levels works against the intraday trend, so trend alignment would reduce signal frequency
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close prices; no bid-ask spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral bias is persistent but round levels shift over time as NIFTY moves to new ranges (24000-25000 becomes 26000-27000). Within a range, the same levels are tested repeatedly.

adaptation_notes: Original strategy used dist < 0.2 absolute for equity stocks priced ~500-5000 INR. Translated to percentage-based distance (pierce_threshold_pct) to work across NIFTY at any price level. Original RSI(14) on 1-min bars → RSI(36) on 5-second bars (3 minutes) for matching the fast exhaustion detection needed at our 30-90s hold horizon — NOT mechanically scaled to 168 bars. Original targeted individual stocks where round numbers (500, 1000) are personal price references; NIFTY/BANKNIFTY round 100-multiples are even stronger because they correspond to option strike levels every 50 points, and every other 100-multiple is a double-anchored round number (24100 = round 100 + round 200). Hold time compressed from 10-25 minutes to 30-90 seconds; stops/targets recalibrated from % moves to absolute option premium points.
weaknesses: NIFTY breaks through round levels cleanly during macro events (FII sell programs, index rebalances) — no news filter in place
Signal fires 4-8 times per day at most — limited throughput relative to pure momentum strategies
RSI(36) on 5-second bars can be noisy during volatile sessions; may generate false oversold readings mid-trend
Near-level condition is binary — no check for HOW MANY times the level has been tested (first test vs fifth test behaves differently)
